classification.difficultyReason: Construct an ordered dice table, restrict it to sum 5, and count outcomes satisfying each condition. Explicitly highlighting the reduced sample space scaffolds the conditional probabilities.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Draw a table showing the sample space if two dice are thrown in turn and their sum is recorded.

inlines.text: Use row headers for the first die and column headers for the second die. Add the two headers to obtain each cell entry. There are 36 equally likely ordered outcomes.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Highlight the reduced sample space if the sum of the two dice is 5.

answer.short: Highlight the four cells for $(1,4)$, $(2,3)$, $(3,2)$ and $(4,1)$.
answer.worked: Highlight every cell containing $5$ in the table from part a. The reduced sample space is $\{(1,4),(2,3),(3,2),(4,1)\}$, with four equally likely ordered outcomes.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Given that the sum of the two dice is 5, what is the probability that:

answer.worked:
Of the four equally likely outcomes $(1,4)$, $(2,3)$, $(3,2)$ and $(4,1)$, only $(1,4)$ has first die $1$.
$$\begin{aligned}P(\text{first die is }1\mid\text{sum is }5)&=\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}$$

children.label: ii
children.prompt: at least one die shows a 1,

answer.worked:
The favourable outcomes are $(1,4)$ and $(4,1)$, out of the four equally likely outcomes with sum $5$.
$$\begin{aligned}P(\text{at least one }1\mid\text{sum is }5)&=\frac{2}{4}\\&=\frac12\end{aligned}$$

children.label: iii
children.prompt: at least one of the dice shows an odd number.

answer.worked:
Each of $(1,4)$, $(2,3)$, $(3,2)$ and $(4,1)$ contains an odd number.
$$\begin{aligned}P(\text{at least one odd number}\mid\text{sum is }5)&=\frac44\\&=1\end{aligned}$$
